description_short: Group semiconductor ALE processes from Sang & Chang Table 1 by activation type and modification/removal chemistry, counting how many distinct semiconductor materials use each combination.

paper.title: Physical and chemical effects in directional atomic layer etching

tables_modeled.label: Table 1
tables_modeled.description: Directional semiconductor ALE processes: semiconductor, modification chemistry, removal chemistry, and activation mode.

properties_used.label: Semiconductor
properties_used.role: Identifies the semiconductor material being etched (e.g., Si, SiO2, Si3N4, III–V).

properties_used.label: Modification
properties_used.role: Describes the surface-modification (adsorption) chemistry used in the first ALE step.

properties_used.label: Removal
properties_used.role: Describes the removal / desorption chemistry used to remove the modified surface layer.

properties_used.label: Activation
properties_used.role: Specifies the activation mode (e.g., ion bombardment, neutral beam, photon/thermal) that drives the ALE process and defines the regime (plasma/ion-assisted vs purely thermal/chemical).

aggregation.description: Rows are grouped by activation label and the combined modification/removal chemistry; for each group, the query counts distinct semiconductor materials.

output_shape.description: One row per (activation, modification/removal chemistry) combination.
columns: activation: activation mode label (e.g., ion-bombardment-assisted, neutral-beam-assisted, thermal).
chemistry_pair: combined string "<modification> / <removal>" summarizing the ALE chemistry.
n_semiconductors: number of distinct semiconductor materials using that activation and chemistry pair.

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The result distinguishes plasma/ion-assisted versus thermal/chemical ALE regimes by their activation labels and shows which modification/removal chemistries are applied across multiple semiconductor materials, revealing dominant and niche process strategies.
